chunks: 3 - He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Hubaysh al-Katib reported to me from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Zafarani, who reported from Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who reported from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Uthman, who reported from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Said, from Fudhayl ibn al-Jad, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, who said:

When Amirul Mu'mineen Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, appointed Muhammad ibn Abu Bakr as the governor of Egypt and its provinces, he wrote him a letter asking him to read it over to the people of Egypt and to act accordingly. The letter said:

In the name of Allah, Most Merciful. From the slave of Allah, Amirul Mu'mineen, Ali ibn Abi Talib, to the people of Egypt and Muhammad ibn Abu Bakr. I convey to you my praise for Allah, other than Whom there is no god.

Secondly, I exhort you to adopt the ways of Taqwa, to be mindful of your duties by guarding against all sins and evils, in all matters for which you are answerable to Him, for unto Him is your return. Surely, Allah, Most High, says: 'Every soul is a hostage to what it has earned' [74:38], and He says: 'Allah warns you to beware of Him, and unto Him is the ultimate return' [3:28]. And He says: 'By your Lord, We shall question them all, regarding what they used to do' [15:92-93].

And know you all, O slaves of Allah! He surely will ask you about all your deeds, small and big. If He punishes we are the wrongdoers, and if He forgives, He is the most Merciful. O slaves of Allah! When a slave acts for Allah in obedience to Him, he draws nearest to earning His pardon and mercy; and recommends him to penitence.

Always adopt Taqwa, be mindful of your duties to Allah by guarding against sins, for that combines all good, the way nothing else does; and leads to the attainment of all good, the way nothing else does, encompassing the good of this world and of hereafter. Allah, Most High, says: 'And it is said to those who fear Allah – what has your Lord revealed? They say: Something good. To those who do good in this world is the good reward, and the hereafter is surely much better. Blessed indeed is the abode of God-fearing' [16:30].

Know you all, O slaves of Allah! A believer acts to earn the reward for three purposes: either it is for the good of this world, then Allah rewards him for his deed in his lifetime. As Allah said for Ibrahim: 'And We gave him his reward in this life, and in the hereafter he shall be among the righteous' [29:27]. So whoever works for Allah, He gives him his reward in this world and the hereafter, and becomes sufficient for him in both abodes. Indeed, Allah says: 'O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. Those who have been bounteous in this world will have a bounty, and Allah's earth is vast. The steadfast will be paid their wages in full without reckoning' [39:10]. And He will not take account for what He gives them here. He says: 'To those who do the good deed is the best reward and more' [10:26]. So the best reward is Paradise, and more is what he is rewarded here. Or he works purely for the next world – for him Allah expiates every sin with good deed. He says: 'Surely, the good deeds will wipe out the evil deeds, and that is a reminder for those who remember' [11:114]. Till on the Day of Judgement, his good deeds will be counted, and Allah will reward him ten fold to seven hundred fold for every single act. Allah says: 'A reward from your Lord, a sufficient gift' [78:36], 'To those who will be meted out the double reward, and they shall be secure in the lofty chambers' [34:37]. So be desirous of this, may Allah have mercy on you, and work hard for it, and urge each other to do accordingly.

And be it known to you all, O slaves of Allah! Those fearing Allah have gained both the instant good of this world and the promised good of hereafter. They share with the people of this world in their worldly gain, for Allah has made it legitimate for them what is necessary from this life. As Allah says: 'Say, who has forbidden Allah's finery which He fashioned for His servants, or the good things He provided? Say: These are meant in the present world, for those who believe, and exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection' [7:32]. They lived on earth the best life, ate the best food, shared with worldly people in their bounties, drank the best of what they drank, wore the best attire, lived in the best abodes, married happily, and rode the best means. Thus they availed of all worldly pleasures, and tomorrow they will be in the proximity of Allah. They will wish and He will grant, will not refuse their prayers, nor reduce their share in eternal bliss.

O servants of Allah! It is this end that the people of wisdom crave, and work for it by adopting Taqwa. And there is no might nor any strength but that from Allah! O servants of Allah! If you fear Allah, and safeguard the rights of your Prophet in respect of the inmates of his house, then you will have surely worshipped Him in the best way, remembered Him in the best manner, expressed gratitude in the best way, adopted the best style of patience and gratitude and the best method of endeavour. Even if someone invokes longer prayers and keeps more fasts, you will be classified as more fearful of Allah and worthiest advisers to those holding divine authority.

O servants of Allah! Be warned of death and its inebriating pang; prepare yourselves for it, for it will rush you into a terrible thing: it will either be good experience with no evil ever accompanying it, or evil experience with no good ever going with it. Who is nearer to Paradise than the one who works for it? And who is nearer to hellfire than the one who works for it? Surely, no soul leaves its body till it has known to which of the two abodes it will reach: Paradise or hellfire. Is he the enemy of Allah or His friend? If he is a friend of Allah, the gates of Paradise will be opened for him, its paths paved, and he will see what Allah has kept ready for him – free from all worries, all burdens lifted. And if he is an enemy of Allah, the gates of hell will be opened for him, its paths paved, and he will find what Allah has prepared for him – all discomfort, deprived of all joy. All this will be at the time of death, and at that moment shall the certitude be. Allah says: 'Those whom the angels will carry off while in state of grace, saying: Peace upon you, enter Paradise for what you did' [16:32]. And He says: 'Those who are carried off by the angels while still wrongdoing themselves; then they will offer submission saying: we did no evil. Yes, Allah surely knows well what you were doing. Enter the gates of hell, abiding therein forever. Wretched indeed is the abode of the arrogant' [16:28-29].

O slaves of Allah! There is no escape from death, so beware of it before it occurs and be prepared. You are being hunted by death; if you stop, it will capture you, and if you flee, it will find you. Its company is more constant than your own shadow! It is tied to your forelocks, and life on earth is being folded from behind you. So remember death frequently, especially when your mind fights you for temptations, for death is a sufficient admonisher. And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, often reminded his companions to remember death, saying: Remember death often, for it demolishes all pleasures and is a barrier between you and your base desires.

O slaves of Allah! That which will happen to the unforgiven one after death is more severe than death itself: the grave! Beware of its constriction, its hardship, its darkness and loneliness. Every day, the grave exclaims: I am the house of loneliness, I am the house of dust; I am the house of gloom, I am the house of insects and vermins. A grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise, or a pit from the pits of hell. When a believing slave is buried, the earth says: Welcome! You were among those I loved when they walked on my back. When you are in my charge, you will see how I deal with you! – then it expands for him as far as one can see. But when an unbeliever is interred, the earth says: You are not welcome! You were among those I hated most. When you are in my charge, you will know how I deal with you! – then it squeezes hard till the ribs come together. Surely, the life of hardship Allah warned about refers to the grave, where He will make the unbeliever victim of ninety-nine dragons which devour his flesh and break his bones, frequenting upon him till resurrection. If only one of those dragons were to blow into the earth, nothing would ever grow from it.

Know you, O slaves of Allah! Your weak spirits and your delicate bodies, for which little discomfort is enough to break down, will be terribly weakened because of this. So if you can have mercy over your bodies and spirits by saving them from what they cannot bear, then act according to what Allah likes, and discard what He dislikes.

O slaves of Allah! The day of resurrection is more severe than the grave. A day when the young will grow old, the old ones get inebriated; wombs will abort, every suckling mother distracted from her child; a dark dreadful day whose evil will be rampant. The angels who have no sins will be scared by the terror of that day, the hard seven skies will tremble, together with the peg-like mountains and the couch-like earth. The heavens will be rent asunder, tottering, turning red like pigment. Mountains shall turn into heaps of sand. The trumpet will be blown, and those in the heavens and earth will be terrified except whoever Allah wills. So what of those who sinned with their ears, eyes, tongue, hand, foot, private parts and stomach – if Allah does not forgive them? For they will be judged and consigned to fire whose pit is deep, heat severe, drink is stinking water, chastisement ever renewed with iron rods. They will not be relieved of its torment nor will the inmates die. An abode where there is no mercy and prayers of the inmates will not be heard.

And know you, O slaves of Allah! Together with this there will be mercy of Allah which will not be thwarted from the slaves – a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for those who fear Allah. Good with no evil accompanying it at any time; its pleasures will never be satiated and its gathering will never disperse. Its inmates will be in proximity of the Merciful, attended by youths with golden saucers containing fruits and sweet basils.

Then know, O Muhammad ibn Abu Bakr! I have appointed you to govern the greatest of my troops in my mind: the people of Egypt. When I have given you that appointment, you deserve most to be cautious about yourself and watchful over your faith. Try your best not to displease your Lord for the sake of people's pleasure, for in Allah's pleasure there is a substitute for everything else, but in anything else there is no substitute for Him. Be severe to the oppressors, censure them. Be lenient to the righteous, bring them closer, and appoint them in your inner circle of brotherhood.

And watch your daily prayers and how you perform them, for you will be leading the people. Therefore you must fulfil all its conditions and not belittle it. Whenever an imam leads prayers with deficiency, he bears the responsibility, while the people following suffer no loss. So fulfil it and guard it – you will earn the same reward as theirs without their reward being reduced.

Then be mindful of your wudu, for it is a condition for the fulfilment of prayers. Wash your mouth three times, draw water in your nose three times, then wash your face, then the right hand, then the left hand, then wipe your head and two feet. Surely, I saw the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, do the same. And know that wudu is half of faith.

Then be watchful about the time of daily prayers. Do not offer them before time because you are free, nor delay them because you are busy. For someone asked the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, about the timings, and the Prophet replied: Jibreel came to me and showed me the timings. He prayed Zuhr when the sun passed the meridian as it declined to his right, then he showed me Asr when the shadows became equal to object size. Then he prayed Maghrib when the sun set, and Isha when the twilight disappeared, and Subh in the last part of the night's darkness near dawn as the stars flickered. So pray on these times, and remain constant on the known tradition and the clear path.

Then look at your ruku and sujud, for the Prophet prayed the most complete prayers, though in practice it was least burdensome. Know that all your affairs follow your prayers – whoever is negligent of his prayers will be more negligent in other acts of worship. I beseech Him Who sees and cannot be seen, and He is on the highest horizon, that He may take us and you among those He loves and is pleased with, so that He may help us remember and praise Him, worship Him best, fulfil His covenant, and in all that He determines in our affairs here and hereafter.

And you, O people of Egypt! Let your speech be confirmed by your conduct, and your public life by your private life. Let not your tongues contradict your hearts. Know that a leader who guides to the right path cannot be equated to one who leads to ruination, nor does the successor of the Prophet compare with his adversary. I am not anxious about a believer or an unbeliever doing you harm – Allah prevents the believer because of his faith, and constrains the unbeliever because of his disbelief. But I worry about the hypocrite, who says what you approve but does what you disapprove.

O Muhammad ibn Abu Bakr, know that the best instruction in religion is piety in the practice of religion and acting in His obedience. I exhort you to be God-fearing in your private and public matters, in any situation. This world is a place of test and tribulation, the hereafter is an abode of reward and eternity. So act for the abode which is forever, turn away from what will perish, but do not forget your portion from the bounties of this world. I enjoin you seven virtues that represent complete Islam: Fear Allah and do not fear people in His presence; The best speech is that confirmed by conduct; Do not give two contradicting judgements in one matter lest your directive become discrepant and you deviate from truth; Love for your subjects what you love for yourself and your family, and detest for them what you detest for yourself, for that establishes authority and benefits the people; Fight in the way of truth and do not fear reproach in the way of Allah; Give good advice when consulted; Make yourself an ideal for Muslims near and far.

May Allah tie us with the bond of love in religion, and adorn us with the adornment of those who fear Allah. May your obedience to Allah subsist till you and I meet as brothers reclining on beds, facing each other in Paradise. O people of Egypt! Do your best to support your governor Muhammad, and remain unflinchingly in your obedience, till you arrive near the Prophet at his Pool. May Allah help you and us on the way of His pleasure. Peace be upon you from Allah and His mercy and blessings.

key_terms.مُنَافِق: Лицемер; тот, кто внешне исповедует ислам, но скрывает неверие

ai.seo_question: Какие указания дал Имам Али Мухаммаду ибн Аби Бакру при назначении его губернатором Египта?
ai.summary: Имам Али (мир ему) написал это всеобъемлющее письмо Мухаммаду ибн Аби Бакру при назначении его губернатором Египта. Письмо содержит наставления о богобоязненности, описания смерти, могилы и Дня Воскресения, указания о молитве и омовении, принципы исламского управления и семь основополагающих исламских принципов.
